messages:
incident-bot: PD page triggered: HIGH error-rate on /v1/generate (service: runtime-proxy) — paging sam as primary oncall :rotating_light:

sam: acked — looking

olivia: pinged sam on call — hearing pager now

sam: quick check: dashboards show a ~2m spike in 5xxs from one router cluster, not global. Query: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{handler="/v1/generate",code=~"5.."}[1m])) by (node)` looks like burst from node-rt-12

ryan: I see the same in router logs, looks like an upstream timeout cascade, maybe a synthetic canary run flooded that node. grabbing logs:```kubectl logs router-rt-12 -n prod --since=5m | grep -i timeout | tail -n 50```

maddy: incident-bot shows PD auto-resolve window closed at +90s earlier today in similar pattern — might be noisy synthetic check we've seen before :thinking_face:

sam: running healthcheck curl against that node: `curl -sS -w '%{http_code}
' https://router-rt-12.internal/_health -o /dev/null` returns 200, latency 180ms. So node recovered. No widespread errors in other clusters.

olivia: any customer-facing errors reported? I can't find any CS tickets or spike in API error rates by customer id in last 10m. looks isolated.

sam: confirmed no request throttles, no quota hits, no Dedicated queue backlog. Latency SLOs fine for majority. marking "customer impact: none" for now.

ryan: suspicious: recent deploy to canary-runner may have created a short traffic surge. checking deploy events: `kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.name=canary-runner -n prod --since=10m` shows a test job started at +3m before spike.

maddy: ok let's silence PD on this alert class for 5m while we dig, so it doesn't wake folks if it flaps again. I'll create a short suppression rule.

maddy: @oncall-bot can you mute escalation key `runtime-proxy-high-5xx` for 300s? :pray:
oncall-bot: Muting rule applied: `runtime-proxy-high-5xx` muted for 5m by maddy — automatic unmute scheduled.

sam: thanks. adding quick notes to the thread and runbook link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/runbooks/runtime-proxy#transient-5xx-bursts

olivia: recommend we add the canary traffic signature to the detection rule (low weight) so synthetic tests don't trigger full PD. Filing a tiny ticket: ENG-ops 1157.

ryan: also posting the grep output for context:
```
2026-03-15T12:01:02Z router-rt-12 timeout waiting for model backend
2026-03-15T12:01:03Z router-rt-12 502 response from model-worker-7
2026-03-15T12:01:04Z router-rt-12 connection reset by peer
```

sam: since this is ephemeral and recovered to green, I'll close the thread after we confirm the suppression and the ticket. If it reappears, we'll escalate to runtime-sre and possibly open a bridge.

maddy: updated the alert rule: added a 60s debounce on that metric stream and lowered per-node sensitivity. will monitor.

olivia: quick postmortem notes: probable cause = synthetic canary generating concentrated traffic to router-rt-12; impact = none to customers; mitigation = short-term mute + debounce + rule tweak; follow-up = ENG-ops 1157 to classify synthetic traffic and score it.

sam: leaving handoff to ryan in 10m — @ryan you'll be second oncall, please watch the muted alerts and unmute if needed.

ryan: on it. I'll keep an eye for 15m, and will escalate if we see >1% global error-rate or CS reports.

incident-bot: PD: page auto-resolved (duration 45s) — no escalation performed.

sam: thanks all. closing thread. :white_check_mark:

ryan: noted; will re-open if it flaps again.

maddy: leaving a short retrospective entry in #postmortems later today.

olivia: thumbs on the follow-up ticket and the runbook tweak. :thumbsup:
